topic:
Sharp minimax detection of conditional average treatment-effect heterogeneity under rough unknown confounding. Observe n iid (X,A,Y), with known X uniform on [0,1]^d, d>=1 fixed, and binary A,Y. Impose consistency and conditional exchangeability; write e(x)=P(A=1|X=x), m0(x)=E[Y|A=0,X=x], m1=m0+tau. For known fixed alpha,beta,gamma in (0,1] and L>=2 require e in H^alpha(L), m0 in H^beta(L), tau in H^gamma(L), and 1/4<=e,m0,m1<=3/4 everywhere. H^s(L) means sup|f|<=L and |f(x)-f(z)|<=L||x-z||_2^s. No true nuisance or nuisance convergence rate is supplied. Test H0: tau is an unknown constant, against D(P)=[integral(tau(x)-integral tau(u)du)^2 dx]^(1/2)>=rho. Define rho_n^* as the infimum rho>0 admitting a measurable randomized test with worst-case null rejection <=.05 and worst-case type-II error <=.2 over the separated alternatives, with empty alternative supremum zero. Determine an explicitly evaluable matching critical-radius rate for every fixed (alpha,beta,gamma,d,L), including any transition logarithms, with constants depending only on these fixed class parameters for all sufficiently large n. Supply a total finite-data attaining test, uniform calibration, tuning and computation cost, and a matching original-fixed-n all-test converse whose null priors EACH have exactly constant tau and whose alternatives satisfy the same original class. On this identical class derive the known-propensity experiment, where the test receives e_P, and characterize exactly when the unknown- and known-propensity radii have the same order. All formulas and the existence of any nuisance penalty are answer-open; smoothness adaptation is not claimed. The full rough-nuisance detection map is the kernel, not pointwise estimation, fixed-alternative power, a regular first-order product-rate theorem or an oracle-only bound. Sanity witness: e=.5+(x1-.5)/16, m0=3/8, tau=1/8+eta*sin(2*pi*x1), |eta|<=1/32, so D=|eta|/sqrt(2), ATE=1/8 and all Bernoulli probabilities satisfy the class; eta=0 is a nonzero homogeneous null. A disclosed known-c channel B|A,Y~Bernoulli(1/4+Y/2-c*A/2) converts tau=c to binary conditional independence; profiling c or importing this reduction alone is not new. Compare precisely against Neykov-Balakrishnan-Wasserman CI testing, PCM 2211.02039, Dukes et al 2410.00985v4, KBRW 2203.00837 and McGrath-Mukherjee 2212.14857 latest version. Consumer: grf::test_calibration and Shiba-Inoue AJE2024 epidemiologic heterogeneity workflows gain a detectability benchmark and a test beyond a fitted forest-score projection; do not claim to certify any existing forest or interpret non-rejection as homogeneity.
PRESOLVE EVIDENCE REQUIRING VERIFICATION: A derived binned covariance identity separates the homogeneous-null bias Cov_bin(e,m0), of order h^(alpha+beta), from the centered effect signal. An explicit fourth-order within-bin statistic estimates the squared covariance and profiles the unknown constant by minimizing a quadratic, without a grid. Its derived variance is bounded by C[Q/n+J/n^2+J^2/n^3+J^3/n^4]. This gives a conservative upper bound throughout the class and a matched oracle-rate region alpha+beta>=gamma, d<=4gamma, including the asymmetric example d=gamma=1, alpha=.1, beta=.9. A known-propensity projection test and fixed-n bump lower argument are supplied. Exact rational checks cover the binned identity, fourth-order expectation and first projection. Every component of a sign-prior null has constant effect and matches a heterogeneous alternative for one observation, but repeated observations expose nuisance moments. Sparse bins, zero curvature, boundary constants, exact-uniform design, and current CI/PCM/nuisance-tuning comparisons were checked; the complete frontier is unproved.
UNRESOLVED BOTTLENECK: Establish sharp multiresolution null calibration and matching fixed-n null-supported mixtures through all sparse regimes, preserving smooth transitions under exact uniform design.
EARLY KILL TEST: At d=gamma=1 and alpha=beta=.1, compute every correction projection and first nonmatching mixture moment; stop a leaking construction or a novelty claim closed by generic transfer.
STRONGEST-FORM DRAFT (unverified, gaps listed inside): <repo-root>/internal/presolve_drafts/stat_cate_homogeneity_testing_nuisance_frontier.md.

open_problems.open_problem: Determine the matching fixed-n minimax separation radius for constant-CATE testing throughout every rough-confounding regime, including separate propensity and baseline-regression elbows and all transition logarithms.

source_refs.excerpt: throughout the strict rough-confounding regime it supplies an upper rate but no nuisance-scale converse
a shared Rademacher prior creates nonzero two-observation cross terms

source_refs.claim: The paper derives the Hölder minimax rate for CATE estimation and a nuisance-driven elbow, but does not determine the global constant-CATE testing radius.
source_refs.author: Edward H. Kennedy, Sivaraman Balakrishnan, James M. Robins, Larry Wasserman

source_refs.claim: The paper supplies asymptotic homogeneity tests over structured rule classes under nuisance-rate conditions, not a sharp Hölder L2 critical-radius map.
source_refs.author: Oliver Dukes, Mats J. Stensrud, Riccardo Brioschi, Aaron Hudson
source_refs.venue: Journal of the American Statistical Association

source_refs.claim: Matching conditional-independence radii are obtained under smooth conditional laws, but with total-variation separation and without separate propensity, baseline, and CATE smoothness.
source_refs.author: Matey Neykov, Sivaraman Balakrishnan, Larry Wasserman

source_refs.claim: The variance-based CATE test resolves null degeneracy using intra-fold splitting and proves asymptotic validity, but does not derive a minimax separation radius over rough Hölder nuisances.
source_refs.author: Fangzhou Yu

open_problems.why_unsolved: The prior CausalSmith run obtained an oracle lower branch, an observational upper envelope, and equality in a relatively smooth region, but its nuisance-supported mixture leaked through repeated observations and could violate the separate baseline Hölder constraint. The web literature closes neighboring problems only: CATE estimation has a nuisance elbow, conditional-independence testing has sharp binned rates under a different separation geometry, and recent CATE-homogeneity tests establish asymptotic validity under supplied nuisance-rate conditions. None controls the competition between centered quadratic CATE signal and propensity-baseline approximation bias across every dense, sparse, and boundary regime while keeping every lower-bound null draw exactly homogeneous.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A piecewise evaluable rate rho_n(alpha,beta,gamma,d), with every equality-case logarithm, a total uniformly calibrated attaining test, and a matching original-fixed-n lower bound supported on legal constant-CATE null laws and separated alternatives in the identical binary Hölder class.

writing_exemplar.why: Its exposition moves from the scientific importance of heterogeneous effects to a precise smooth experiment and a nuisance-driven minimax phase diagram.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: CATE heterogeneity matters for individualized decisions -> existing procedures do not reveal fundamental limits -> smooth causal nuisances create minimax elbows -> global homogeneity testing requires its own complete detection map

method_exemplars.technique: Binned degenerate U-statistics with uniform error control and matching mixture lower bounds under smooth conditional laws.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Binary treatment and outcome make each covariate bin a small conditional table, but the destination must replace conditional-independence distance with centered CATE energy and separate nuisance smoothness.

method_exemplars.technique: Proxy-functional statistics and moment-matched mixture converses for a constancy test contaminated by an unknown rough mean.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The same structural conflict arises between a quadratic heterogeneity signal and nuisance-induced bias, although the causal Bernoulli likelihood adds treatment selection.

method_exemplars.technique: Localized fuzzy hypotheses and localized higher-order influence-function corrections under separate causal nuisance smoothness.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It uses the identical propensity, outcome-regression, and CATE factorization and exposes the smoothness interactions that testing must recompute.

open_problems.open_problem: Characterize exactly when revealing the true propensity score leaves the constant-CATE minimax detection radius unchanged and when unknown propensity produces a strictly larger radius, including asymmetric smoothness regimes and boundary logarithms.

source_refs.excerpt: promote the known-versus-unknown-propensity comparison to a separate iff phase-boundary theorem
At which derived smoothness frontier does the observational separation radius cease to equal the known-propensity rate?

source_refs.claim: For regular ATE estimation, propensity-score knowledge does not improve the semiparametric efficiency bound, providing a benchmark that need not extend to nonregular heterogeneity detection.
source_refs.author: Jinyong Hahn

source_refs.claim: Unknown propensity and outcome-regression smoothness jointly create a minimax CATE-estimation elbow, but known- and unknown-propensity homogeneity-testing experiments are not compared.
source_refs.author: Edward H. Kennedy, Sivaraman Balakrishnan, James M. Robins, Larry Wasserman

source_refs.claim: Known propensity weakens some nuisance conditions in the paper's asymptotic theory, but no minimax comparison of the two experiments is provided.
source_refs.author: Oliver Dukes, Mats J. Stensrud, Riccardo Brioschi, Aaron Hudson
source_refs.venue: Journal of the American Statistical Association

open_problems.why_unsolved: Regular ATE ancillarity does not settle a null-degenerate global test. With known propensity, exact treatment residuals are available; with unknown propensity, fine-scale variation in treatment assignment can imitate or cancel the covariance signal used to detect CATE variation. The prior run established a known-propensity exponent and an observational no-penalty region, but outside that region retained only an oracle-submodel converse. A necessary-and-sufficient result therefore requires the observational testing modulus itself, rather than importing a first-order nuisance product-rate threshold.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A paired minimax result giving explicit known-propensity and unknown-propensity critical radii on the same class, plus a necessary-and-sufficient inequality in alpha,beta,gamma,d for their ratio to stay bounded above and below.

writing_exemplar.why: Its organizing question is the statistical value of knowing the propensity score, furnishing the right contrast for the nonregular testing problem.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Ignorability introduces an assignment nuisance -> knowing assignment appears informationally valuable -> regular ATE efficiency can nevertheless be unchanged -> determine the exact equality frontier for nonregular CATE-homogeneity detection

method_exemplars.technique: Switch nuisance perturbations on and off within localized fuzzy-hypothesis constructions and compare oracle and nuisance-limited balances.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The same causal factorization permits a direct comparison of subexperiments, after replacing pointwise estimation loss by global testing risk.

method_exemplars.technique: Poissonized bin counts and weighted degenerate U-statistics whose variance reflects local sample availability.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The binwise argument can isolate the extra task of learning assignment probabilities and determine when it changes the critical-radius order.

method_exemplars.technique: Target-specific over- and undersmoothing with explicit comparisons across nuisance smoothness and sample-splitting regimes.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It demonstrates that prediction-optimal propensity tuning need not be target-optimal, a likely mechanism behind any gap between the two testing experiments.

open_problems.open_problem: Derive sharp multiresolution null calibration for profiled fourth-order CATE-energy statistics across dense and sparse-bin regimes, determining whether the unavoidable cross-resolution price is bounded, iterated-logarithmic, or logarithmic.

source_refs.excerpt: bounding the joint coefficient covariance and the profiling remainder uniformly when both sieve ranks exceed n
Determine when the width is sqrt(log K_n), sqrt(log log K_n), or bounded.

source_refs.claim: A weighted multiresolution U-statistic is nearly minimax for Wasserstein conditional-independence testing, but it does not handle a profiled CATE-energy statistic or separate causal nuisances.
source_refs.author: Matey Neykov, Larry Wasserman, Ilmun Kim, Sivaraman Balakrishnan

source_refs.claim: The paper gives finite-sample Type-I and Type-II control with explicit smoothing for Sobolev regression testing, but not for confounded causal heterogeneity.
source_refs.author: Yun Yang, Zuofeng Shang, Guang Cheng

source_refs.claim: The homogeneity tests use asymptotic multiplier-bootstrap calibration over structured rule classes rather than fixed-n multiresolution calibration over a Hölder ball.
source_refs.author: Oliver Dukes, Mats J. Stensrud, Riccardo Brioschi, Aaron Hudson
source_refs.venue: Journal of the American Statistical Association

open_problems.why_unsolved: At fine resolutions, many exact-uniform bins contain fewer observations than the order of the required covariance statistic; at coarse resolutions, the homogeneous-null bias from the propensity and baseline regression dominates. Each coordinate is also a profiled degenerate fourth-order statistic, not the nondegenerate first-order score handled by the donor growing-resolution proposal. Consequently the degeneracy order, covariance, and profiling remainder all vary with occupancy, and neither coordinatewise union bounds nor a first-order multiplier bootstrap identifies the correct cross-scale price.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: An explicit cross-resolution semimetric and computable critical-value rule, with fixed-n uniform null tails, separated-alternative power at the sharp radius, declared transition factors, and runtime and memory bounds throughout dense and sparse occupancy regimes.

writing_exemplar.why: It begins from impossibility without regularity, formulates a smooth restricted experiment, and treats implementability and calibration as part of the minimax result.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Unrestricted conditional testing is impossible -> smoothness enables nontrivial detection -> binning produces an implementable minimax test -> rough-confounding CATE testing requires aggregation that remains valid in sparse bins

method_exemplars.technique: Weighted aggregation of resolution-specific degenerate U-statistics with scale-dependent thresholds.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The destination likewise crosses occupancy regimes, but adds fourth-order nuisance correction and an estimated centering constant.

method_exemplars.technique: Nonasymptotic level allocation over a finite family of U-statistic squared-distance tests.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It provides a direct template for aggregating oracle quadratic tests, while the causal destination requires sharper dependence and occupancy analysis.

method_exemplars.technique: Second-order pathwise differentiation and degenerate U-statistic calibration at a null asserting equality of unknown functions.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It supplies close causal null-degeneracy machinery, though not triangular multiresolution covariance for a fourth-order statistic.

open_problems.open_problem: Determine whether a treatment-weighted local cross-product proxy can improve the rough-nuisance constant-CATE detection rate over corrected direct CATE-energy estimation under unrestricted bounded Bernoulli outcome laws.

source_refs.excerpt: Can a treatment-weighted local cross-product proxy improve on corrected direct CATE-energy estimation

open_problems.why_unsolved: The source proposal identifies Kotekal and Kundu's squared-first-difference proxy as the donor construction, but its first identity fails after treatment selection: unknown propensity weighting, asymmetric treatment-arm regressions, and unrestricted conditional Bernoulli noise leave a product of propensity and baseline projection residuals. The donor's roughest-regime improvement also exploits Gaussian noise information unavailable in the destination class, so the method cannot be transferred without a new observable identity or a proof that no such improvement is possible.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: Either a proxy-functional test with a phasewise sharp separation radius and a matching lower bound on the same Bernoulli causal class, or a regime-specific impossibility result showing that unrestricted bounded outcome noise prevents improvement over corrected direct energy.

writing_exemplar.why: It frames CATE variance as the omnibus target and isolates nonlinear nuisance bias and degeneracy under homogeneity.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: CATE dispersion is a natural omnibus heterogeneity measure -> direct variance inference degenerates under homogeneity -> nuisance correction becomes nonlinear -> ask whether an observable proxy has better rough-confounding behavior

method_exemplars.technique: Replace direct variance-function distance by a squared-difference proxy and match its rate using moment-matched lower mixtures.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Both problems test constancy of a conditional function in the presence of a distinct rough conditional-mean nuisance.

method_exemplars.technique: Construct nuisance-adjusted higher-order U-statistics at a degenerate causal functional null.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It supplies the direct causal-energy benchmark that a proposed proxy would need to beat or match.

method_exemplars.technique: Truncated higher-order influence-function correction with explicit approximation-bias and stochastic-variance control.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The destination proxy is a nonlinear causal functional in precisely the regime where first-order nuisance products are too large.

open_problems.open_problem: Over compact ranges of propensity, baseline-regression, and CATE smoothness, determine the minimax adaptation penalty for constant-CATE detection when none of alpha, beta, or gamma is supplied.

source_refs.claim: The optimal Hölder CATE-estimation tuning depends on unknown smoothness, and the paper identifies data-driven adaptation as a natural next step without resolving it.
source_refs.author: Edward H. Kennedy, Sivaraman Balakrishnan, James M. Robins, Larry Wasserman

source_refs.claim: For classical nonparametric signal detection over unknown smoothness, adaptation without loss is impossible and an iterated-logarithm price is unavoidable.
source_refs.author: Vladimir G. Spokoiny

source_refs.claim: Weighted multiresolution aggregation yields nearly minimax conditional-independence testing across scales, but does not adapt simultaneously to three causal smoothness indices or identify the sharp penalty.
source_refs.author: Matey Neykov, Larry Wasserman, Ilmun Kim, Sivaraman Balakrishnan

open_problems.why_unsolved: Classical adaptive signal detection has one unknown signal regularity and a simple null, whereas rough-confounding CATE detection has three smoothness indices and the identity of the rate-limiting nuisance changes across the phase diagram. A multiscale maximum must therefore adapt simultaneously to signal resolution, correction rank, and nuisance asymmetry while retaining size under a composite, degenerate null. Existing adaptive-testing lower bounds do not determine whether this enlarged search costs only log log n, a larger logarithm, or different penalties on different phase boundaries.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: An adaptive critical-radius family indexed by the true alpha,beta,gamma, a single fully data-driven uniformly level test attaining it over a declared compact smoothness rectangle, and a matching adaptive lower bound identifying every unavoidable logarithmic penalty.

writing_exemplar.why: Its phase-diagram presentation makes the practical dependence of optimal tuning on unknown causal smoothness transparent.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Optimal causal rates vary across nuisance and target smoothness -> oracle tuning requires those indices -> practical procedures do not know them -> characterize the exact price of adapting the homogeneity test

method_exemplars.technique: Wavelet multiscale testing paired with a lower mixture proving the iterated-logarithm adaptation cost.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It is the canonical statement-and-proof template for distinguishing an unavoidable adaptive penalty from a loose multiple-testing correction.

method_exemplars.technique: Weighted aggregation of U-statistics across resolutions under conditional smoothness.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Its multiresolution construction is structurally close to the scale search needed for CATE detection, before adding nuisance-correction ranks.

method_exemplars.technique: Finite-family aggregation of quadratic U-tests with nonasymptotic level control and oracle comparison.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It provides a finite-data route to combine resolution-specific energy tests while preserving an explicit error budget.

literature_map:
Kennedy, Balakrishnan, Robins and Wasserman (AoS 2024, arXiv:2203.00837v4) derive the Hölder minimax CATE-estimation rate, a nuisance-driven elbow, localized fuzzy lower bounds, and localized HOIF attainability; global constant-CATE detection is not characterized.
Dukes, Stensrud, Brioschi and Hudson (JASA 2026, arXiv:2410.00985v4) directly test quantitative and qualitative treatment-effect heterogeneity, but use structured rule classes, asymptotic calibration, and nuisance-rate conditions rather than a full Hölder minimax frontier.
Yu (arXiv:2607.17451, 2026) targets CATE variance and resolves null degeneracy through intra-fold sample splitting, but supplies asymptotic inference rather than sharp minimax detection rates.
Lapenta, Strittmatter and Vergara Merino (arXiv:2607.06412, 2026) give an ML-compatible omnibus test across several causal designs, again without the requested rough-nuisance critical-radius map.
Lundborg, Kim, Shah and Samworth (AoS 2024, arXiv:2211.02039v4) prove minimax power for projected conditional covariance; the causal constant-CATE null adds profiling and a second nuisance geometry.
Neykov, Balakrishnan and Wasserman (AoS 2021, arXiv:2001.03039v4) obtain matching smooth conditional-independence radii using implementable binned U-statistics and mixture converses, but under total-variation separation and without the e/m0/tau factorization.
Neykov, Wasserman, Kim and Balakrishnan (Information and Inference 2024, arXiv:2308.08672) add a weighted multiresolution U-statistic and nearly minimax Wasserstein rates, providing a sparse/dense aggregation template.
McGrath and Mukherjee (forthcoming AoS, arXiv:2212.14857v5) show that rough-Hölder doubly robust estimation can require deliberate nuisance over- or undersmoothing; their target remains regular functional estimation.
Kotekal and Kundu (AoS 2025, arXiv:2310.12424v3) solve an analogous constancy test behind an unknown rough mean and show that a proxy statistic can outperform naive quadratic estimation.
Yang, Shang and Cheng (COLT 2020) provide explicit finite-sample error control and smoothing for Sobolev regression testing, but not for binary causal data or a composite homogeneous-effect null.
Robins, Li, Tchetgen Tchetgen and van der Vaart supply higher-order influence-function and U-statistic machinery for non-root-n causal functionals; Liu, Mukherjee, Newey and Robins develop empirical HOIF kernels that weaken density requirements.
Hahn (Econometrica 1998) proves propensity-score ancillarity for regular ATE efficiency, while Zhou and Zhu (JSPI 2021) compare true and estimated propensity for CATE estimation; neither addresses nonregular homogeneity detection.
Crump, Hotz, Imbens and Mitnik and Dai, Shen and Stern provide earlier nonparametric or U-statistic homogeneity tests, but not a sharp all-smoothness observational radius.
Shiba and Inoue (AJE 2024) caution that grf::test_calibration assesses calibration relative to a fitted score rather than certifying the true causal effect, motivating a separate detectability benchmark.
Targeted searches found no paper closing the fixed-n all-smoothness CATE-homogeneity frontier or the exact known-versus-unknown propensity equality region.
prior_proposal_map:
The highest-yield source was banked qid stat_cate_heterogeneity_testing_frontier/v1, a near-identical constant-CATE minimax run whose README and writeup leave the strict rough-confounding converse, separate alpha/beta elbows, and transition logarithms open.
All three angle reviews for that run were inspected; angle0_v3 supplied explicit strengthening paths for ranks exceeding n and for an iff known-versus-unknown-propensity theorem.
Its proto_core seed ledger preserved credible unselected directions including proxy energy, aligned-versus-dense hybrid power, growing-dimensional null spaces, and adaptive smoothness.
Banked stat_cate_local_overlap_nuisance_frontier/v1 independently records the same full-support Bernoulli-mixture failure: one-observation cancellation leaves nonzero two-observation cross terms.
Banked stat_causal_resolution_growingk_frontier/v1 supplies a technique donor for intrinsic cross-resolution covariance width while documenting unresolved positive-noise observational calibration.
Accepted stat_discrete_ate_heterogeneity_frontier/v1 was inspected for sparse occupancy, collision, and fixed-n mixture machinery; its scalar ATE-estimation target makes it a technique source rather than a duplicate.
Downgraded stat_plm_two_nuisance_minimax/v1 was inspected as a scope guard: product-rate converses can collapse on degenerate covariate subclasses, reinforcing the need for an exact same-class lower experiment.
No archived angle-rejected core exists in the near-identical CATE-testing run; rejected content is retained through proto_core seed_details and reviewer JSONs.
